title: The Unsent, Plantation
statement: Mara planted one core and it rooted. I am an archivist; one of anything is a sample, six is a holding. So the vessel has been cored five times more, and six strips stand in a row in the soil to the right, each cut to a different length because each was taken from a different depth, each with the same thirty-five bands and each already sprouting from its top year. The vessel is a scarred thing now, five pale slots across its rings, still standing, still legible. I did not ask whether a letter can survive being read this many times. The row answers it. Whoever comes next can thin the plantation, or wait for the first of the six to flower.
process: I kept the parent's vessel, rings, pith, soil band and the planted core with its roots and shoot, then repeated the core as six strips of different heights set in a row, each with roots below the soil line and a two-leaf shoot above, and cut five pale scar slots through the vessel's rings where the cores came from. The vessel was moved left to make room.
